# 01 - LFP, LMFP, and Phosphate-Family Lithium-Ion Batteries

Acquisition method: Web research note synthesized from public sources.

Primary sources:

- IEA, Global EV Outlook 2025, Electric vehicle batteries: https://www.iea.org/reports/global-ev-outlook-2025/electric-vehicle-batteries
- IEA, Global EV Outlook 2024, Trends in electric vehicle batteries: https://www.iea.org/reports/global-ev-outlook-2024/trends-in-electric-vehicle-batteries
- NHTSA, Electric and Hybrid Vehicles: Battery, Charging & Safety: https://www.nhtsa.gov/vehicle-safety/electric-and-hybrid-vehicles

## What It Is

LFP means lithium iron phosphate. It is a lithium-ion chemistry using an iron-phosphate cathode, typically paired with graphite anodes. LMFP or LFMP adds manganese to the phosphate cathode family to raise voltage and energy density while preserving much of the low-cost, cobalt-free appeal of LFP.

## Automotive Relevance Today

LFP is one of the two dominant EV cathode families today, alongside NMC/NCA high-nickel lithium-ion. IEA reports that LFP made up nearly half of the global EV battery market in 2024. China is the center of LFP production and adoption; LFP reached very high shares in China and is growing in Europe, while remaining below 10% in the United States in 2024.

LFP is especially relevant for:

- Lower-cost EVs.
- Standard-range trims.
- Fleet and high-utilization vehicles.
- Vehicles where long cycle life and lower fire risk are more important than maximum range.
- Markets where low cost matters more than extreme cold-weather or high-speed driving range.

## Strengths

LFP's main advantage is cost. IEA says LFP packs are almost 30% cheaper per kWh than NMC packs, while NMC still has higher energy density. LFP avoids nickel and cobalt, lowering raw-material cost exposure and reducing supply-chain and ESG risk.

LFP is also valued for cycle life, thermal stability, and usable state of charge. IEA notes that LFP can be charged to 100% when required without the same degradation concern that leads many NMC systems to recommend daily charging only to around 80%.

## Weaknesses

LFP's disadvantages are lower energy density and weaker cold-weather performance. IEA reports LFP pack energy density is about one-fifth lower by mass and about one-third lower by volume than NMC packs. That matters for premium vehicles, large SUVs, trucks, towing, and packaging-constrained cars.

Cold-weather performance is a recurring limitation. LFP can lose power and charging performance in low temperatures unless the vehicle has strong thermal management.

## Future Development

LMFP/LFMP and CATL-style M3P phosphate-family batteries aim to fill the gap between LFP and NMC. The idea is to raise energy density and voltage while retaining lower material cost and reduced critical-mineral exposure. IEA notes ongoing efforts to increase manganese content in both NMC and LFP-related chemistries.

## Commercialization Outlook

LFP is fully commercial and scaling. LMFP and related phosphate variants are near-term improvements rather than distant future bets. They are likely to appear first in Chinese-market vehicles and mid-range global models, then diffuse outward if licensing, tariffs, and supply-chain localization permit.

## Implications for Older EV Value

LFP's rise could pressure resale values of older short-range NMC EVs if buyers perceive LFP as cheaper, safer, longer-lived, and good enough. However, high-range NMC vehicles may retain value where energy density and winter performance matter. LFP-equipped used cars may age well if battery health and charging behavior remain strong.
